The absense of appreciation for our own viscera could be the cause of 
atrocities around the world, but how do we stop looking at ourselves, 
our own flesh and blood with such distaste? I believe if we had a
 true kinship with our internals, we would be a more responsible society. 
This mobile explores the concept of the visceral in the anthropocene, 
intertwined with the earth, and all of its inhabitants.   

Made up of bioplastics made from agar and bacteria, 
found objects, metals, and clay, the mobile itself acts as a 
screen to expose visuals of the earth through a damaged lens.

Your Project Description (max 2000 chara: You know the moment: you lock eyes with your best friend across the room when something happens, a quick glance that says a million words. The expressions we make with our eyes and eyebrows can tell a story and reveal the unspoken. Sometimes it’s surprise, surprise that morphs into joy, or shock, or disappointment. Maybe disgust, annoyance, or anger. Maybe you’re thinking of a fond memory, or it’s laced with sadness, with contemplation. As you go about your day, you experience countless emotions — it’s what you choose to display that can then be decoded. As you move your mouse across the screen, you can bring forward a variety of emotions, morphing from one to the next.

Your Project Description (max 2000 chara: Butterfly Dance explores how personal birthday information can be encrypted through cryptography and then transformed into visual work through visual rules and generative code. I really like butterflies, so I chose the butterfly as the main visual element. I divided the butterfly into five variables: upper wings, lower wings, body, antennae, and color, and used numerical codes to control these different visual features. The project began with a “birthday cryptography” system: each person’s birthday is converted into a set of numbers, and these numbers determine the different forms of the butterfly. As a result, each person can enter their birthday and generate a butterfly of their own.
File 1 description: This video shows a butterfly generator in motion. The program randomizes the antennae, upper wings, lower wings, and color, creating a different butterfly each time within the same visual system.
File 2 description: This poster combines p5.js and Illustrator. I used p5.js to generate different butterfly forms, then added gradients, textures, patterns, and colors in Illustrator. The project explores how code controls form while Illustrator develops visual style and personality.
File 3 description: I used if and else if statements to change the appearance of a single variable. Different value ranges produce different upper-wing shapes, allowing one variable to control multiple visual outcomes.
Anyone's work inspired you at the open c: Yes. I got a lot of new inspiration from my classmates’ work during the open class. One student explored different vase forms, which I found visually very interesting. Another student visualized the different ingredients they used when making chai, which also left a strong impression on me. Some students used circles of different sizes to represent words of different lengths in a text, while others experimented with turning audio into visual images. These projects showed me that the same kind of information can be transformed and expressed through very different visual systems, and they gave me many new ideas.
